label: Late copy-phase steps (t>=12) when the fed-back input is one of 0/r/b/d/p/c/3/o
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never on original-token or <DEL> steps, and essentially never before recall_idx 3. The firing rate climbs with absolute step t: about 5% of steps at t=12-15 and about 12% at t=17, so it is concentrated in long sequences (L=9 holds 64% of the mass). Within those steps it prefers particular fed-back input tokens: 0 (5.9x lift), r, b, d, p, c, and more weakly 3 and o. There is also a weaker preference for output tokens j and i and for previous inputs i, m, 0, r. The predicate (copy, t>=12, in_tok in that set) covers about 74% of activation mass on dev but has only about 16% precision. Most late-copy steps with those inputs do not fire, and adding output, previous-token, L or repeat-count conditions did not raise F1 above about 0.28. Whatever decides firing at a given step is not captured by single-step token identity. Activations are tiny (max 0.011). Top-quartile activations are somewhat better covered (79%) than bottom-quartile ones (60%).
